options.text: 36pi, 72pi and 256pi, from squaring the radius of each sphere.

12pi, 9pi and 32pi square metres, from using the sphere radius as the area.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.topic: Why a surface must be oriented
questions.learningObjective: Explain why reversing a surface orientation reverses the sign of flux.
questions.stem: The planning memo states that a flux figure changes sign if the surface orientation is reversed. Explain why orientation matters.

answer.exemplar: Flux is defined with respect to a chosen normal direction, so reversing the orientation flips the sign of every contribution and hence of the total. The physics of the flow does not change; only the bookkeeping of what counts as entering and what counts as leaving does. That is why a closed surface is always given the outward orientation before a divergence theorem is applied.

questions.explanation: Flux is defined with respect to a chosen unit normal, so reversing the orientation negates every contribution. Only the convention for entering and leaving reverses, not the field.
questions.hint: Flux is measured along a chosen normal.

questions.stem: The memo notes that flux through a sphere in a radial field needs no integration. Explain why.

answer.exemplar: A radial field points along the radius, so at every point of the sphere it is exactly perpendicular to the surface. questions.explanation: A radial field is perpendicular to a sphere everywhere, so F dot n is the constant strength and the integral collapses to strength times 4pi R squared, with no cancellation anywhere.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why a vertical field over a plaza gives strength times area.
questions.stem: The memo explains why a vertical field over a horizontal plaza gives a flux equal to the plaza area times the field strength. Give that explanation.

answer.exemplar: A vertical field makes an angle of ninety degrees with the horizontal plaza, so the component of the field along the surface normal is the whole field strength and nothing is lost to obliqueness. The flux integrand F dot n dS therefore reduces to the strength times dA, and integrating over the plaza gives the strength multiplied by the plaza area, with no dependence on the shape of the plaza at all.

questions.explanation: The vertical field is perpendicular to the plaza, so the component along the normal is the full strength and F dot n dS reduces to strength times dA. Integrating gives strength times area.
questions.hint: Perpendicular fields leave nothing to project.

answer.exemplar: For a vertical field the integrand F dot n dS reduces to the field strength times the vertical component of the unit normal times dS, and the vertical component of the normal times dS is exactly the area of the base region beneath the roof. questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.topic: Dropping the square root
questions.learningObjective: Explain why the square root in the area element cannot be dropped.
questions.stem: The memo cautions staff that forgetting the square root is the most common slip. Explain why the square root is unavoidable.

answer.exemplar: The area element of a graph is the magnitude of the cross product of the two tangent vectors, and a magnitude is a square root by definition. The two tangent vectors are perpendicular to each other in the horizontal directions, so their cross product has components f_x, f_y and 1, and the length of that vector is sqrt(1 + f_x^2 + f_y^2). Writing the sum without the root would give the squared length, not the length itself.

questions.explanation: The area element is the length of the cross product of the two tangent vectors, and a length is a square root by definition. The sum 1 + f_x^2 + f_y^2 is only the squared length.
questions.hint: A length is a square root by definition.

questions.learningObjective: Explain how a flux figure differs from a local field value.
questions.stem: A memo contrast asks the group to explain how a flux figure differs from the size of the field at a single point. Give that explanation.

answer.exemplar: A flux figure is obtained by integrating the field against the oriented area element, so it is a total that depends on the field strength, the area and the orientation together. The size of the field at one point is a local quantity with no area attached. Comparing the two numbers is meaningless, because they measure different things and carry different units.

questions.explanation: Flux integrates the field over an oriented surface and gives a total, while the field at a point is local and carries no area. The two have different dimensions.
questions.hint: One is a total, the other is local.
